facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 8:00 AM ET

The 2026 VidantaWorld Mexico Open begins Thursday at Vidanta Vallarta — and it arrives with one of the most compelling storyline setups of any tournament this fall.

Here's what you need to know before Round 1:

📍 Venue: Vidanta Vallarta, Mexico
💰 Purse: $6 million
🏆 Points: 500 FedExCup Fall points for the winner
🗓️ Schedule: Thursday, October 29 through Sunday, November 1

WHO TO WATCH:
🏌️ Wyndham Clark — the pre-tournament favorite, already a three-time winner this season
🏌️ Brian Campbell — defending champion (+22500 odds to repeat)
🏌️ Brandon Smotherman — won his last TWO events; arrives eyeing an unprecedented three in a row
🏌️ Tony Finau, Max Homa, Tom Kim — deep field of proven tour players

COURSE UPDATE: Holes 4, 11, 13, and 15 at Vidanta Vallarta have all been reworked heading into this year's event. The course plays differently from past editions, and players who have studied the changes could have a significant advantage early in the week.

This is one of the most exciting opening-week setups we've seen all fall. Who do you have winning? 👇

stories.title: Brandon Smotherman's Stunning Run — Can He Win Three PGA Tour Events in a Row? [TIER 1]

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Brandon Smotherman has won his last TWO PGA Tour events.

Now he tees it up at the VidantaWorld Mexico Open.

Three in a row would be one of the most remarkable stretches in modern golf. Can he do it? 🏆 #PGATour

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Bermuda Championship playoff: won.
Previous October title: won.
Mexico Open: next.

Smotherman is the most in-form player in golf right now. #PGATour #SmothermanWatch

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 8:00 AM ET

Brandon Smotherman is officially the hottest golfer on the PGA Tour.

He won last week. He won the week before that. Now he's walking onto the first tee at Vidanta Vallarta with a chance to become one of a very small group of players in the modern era to win THREE consecutive PGA Tour events.

This isn't just a streak — it's a statement. Smotherman has been consistent, he's been clutch (he won Bermuda in a Monday playoff), and he's proven that he can back it up when the pressure rises.

Three consecutive wins is the kind of rare stretch that gets your name etched into golf history books. Tiger Woods did it. A handful of others have come close in recent years. Smotherman has his chance starting tomorrow.

Are you watching? Because this is must-see golf. ⛳
facebook.image_caption: Two wins in a row. A third would be historic. Smotherman arrives at the Mexico Open as the sport's hottest story. 🔥 #PGATour

LPGA Maybank Championship starts TOMORROW in Kuala Lumpur.

Yamashita (defending), Yin (course record holder), Haeran Ryu (No. 3 ranked) all in the field.

The LPGA Asia swing ends with a stacked final tournament. 🌏 #LPGA

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 10:30 AM ET

The LPGA Maybank Championship starts tomorrow in Kuala Lumpur — and the field is as strong as any event on the tour's Asian swing.

🌏 Venue: Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club, West Course, Malaysia
🗓️ Dates: October 29 – November 1, 2026

TOP PLAYERS TO WATCH:
🏌️ No. 3 Haeran Ryu — one of the most consistent players in women's golf
🏌️ No. 4 Miyu Yamashita — DEFENDING champion (won in a playoff last year at -18)
🏌️ No. 5 Ruoning Yin — holds the tournament RECORD (-23 in 2024)
🏌️ No. 7 Lottie Woad — rapidly ascending in the world rankings
🏌️ No. 8 Charley Hull — one of the tour's most popular and exciting players

This event has delivered some spectacular champions in recent years. With Yamashita defending and Yin holding the course record, expect a competitive final round. The LPGA Asia swing wraps up after this week — it ends with a worthy finale.

Which player are you following this week? 🌏 #LPGA #MaybankChampionship

stories.title: John Daly II Headlines Mexico Open Amateur Story — Following His Father's Legend [TIER 2]

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
John Daly II tees off Thursday at the VidantaWorld Mexico Open (10:44 AM ET).

A famous surname. A personal story. And an entirely different chapter of golf.

Keep an eye on Daly II this week. ⛳ #PGATour #MexicoOpen

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 1:00 PM ET

There's a name in the VidantaWorld Mexico Open field that will turn heads.

John Daly II tees off Thursday at 10:44 AM ET.

The son of one of golf's most colorful and beloved champions, John Daly II has been carving out his own story in professional golf — one that is entirely his own, even if the surname carries weight the moment he steps to the first tee.

What makes his journey compelling is exactly that tension: a famous golf name, a famous golf swing, and a young man working to define himself on his own terms. Playing in a PGA Tour event alongside tour veterans and established stars, Daly II gets a stage this week that most players at his stage of development don't see.

Whether he contends or not is secondary to the story. Golf loves a legacy moment — and there's something undeniably compelling about watching the next generation carry a name that means something to the sport.

Good luck to John Daly II this week. ⛳

stories.title: Five Key Storylines for the VidantaWorld Mexico Open [TIER 2]

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Five reasons to watch the Mexico Open this week:

1. Smotherman's three-peat chase
2. Wyndham Clark at his best
3. New course layout at Vidanta Vallarta
4. John Daly II in the field
5. Hojgaard as a sleeper to watch

Starts TOMORROW. ⛳ #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Posting Window: 3:30 PM ET

Five reasons why the VidantaWorld Mexico Open might be the most compelling tournament of the fall season:

1️⃣ SMOTHERMAN'S THREE-PEAT: He's won back-to-back PGA Tour events. Three straight would be one of the rarest streaks in the modern game. This is the story of the week.

2️⃣ WYNDHAM CLARK AT HIS PEAK: Three wins this season. The favorite heading in. Clark has the kind of form that wins tournaments even when the competition is this deep.

3️⃣ A NEW-LOOK COURSE: Holes 4, 11, 13, and 15 at Vidanta Vallarta have all been redesigned. First-round ball-striking stats will tell us a lot about who adapted best to the changes.

4️⃣ JOHN DALY II IN THE FIELD: The legacy storyline gets real this week. Daly II tees off Thursday with one of golf's most recognizable surnames and something to prove.

5️⃣ RASMUS HOJGAARD AS A SLEEPER: The PGA Tour expert picks flagged Hojgaard at +6600 as a potential surprise. Keep his name in mind if the leaderboard starts shifting Saturday afternoon.

Who wins? Drop your pick below. 👇 #PGATour #MexicoOpen
